items.title: A tail of a quasi-regular sequence is quasi-regular modulo the earlier elements
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that if f_1, ..., f_c is an M-quasi-regular sequence, then the tail f_{i+1}, ..., f_c is quasi-regular for M modulo the earlier elements (statement lines 17243-17251). The proof does not redo the definition: it reduces to the case of one element, rewrites the graded pieces of the quotient module as quotients of the graded pieces of M, and isolates the intersection identity J^n M intersected with f_1 M equal to f_1 J^{n-1}M, which it verifies from the assumption that the associated graded of M is a polynomial algebra (proof lines 17253-17274). Locating the crux in that single intersection is the content of the argument, and the author writes both reductions out. H2.
